title: SPEED 2 –preoperative and perioperative psychological interventions which aim to further decrease the duration of hospital stay and increase the performance status of patients undergoing surgeries
summary:
Prehabilitation prior to surgery is becoming more frequently used. There is no debate on its vital importance for surgery. However, the  specific aspect of prehabilitation have not yet been fully understood. The psychosocial and mental health aspect in prehabilitation and its connection the postoperative performance has not yet been sufficiently shown. 

We postulate that patients who will undergo preoperative and perioperative a psychological short-intervention will leave the hospital at an earlier time point. They will perform better in objective measurements of physical fitness as compared to patients who will undergo the current standard of care regardless of the surgical Intervention.

interventions.name: Training for a sense of self achievement: Mastery Experiences intervention (reflection exercise)
Training with vicarious experiences intervention (podcast) + Verbal persuasion intervention (podcast)
Training with psychoeducation about emotional stress: Physiological arousal (relaxation exercises)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing elective Surgery (Predefined Surgeries)
Informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
diagnosed psychiatric disease
IV- drug abuse
Alcohol abuse
Performance status > ECOG I
